title: Password hashing in 60 seconds
caption: Password hashing in 60 seconds: why good sites never store your password, and how they still check it.

scenes.say: If a site stores passwords as they are, one breach leaks every one of them.
So good sites store a hash instead.

items.title: Hash
items.text: one way: easy in, no way back
items.say: A hash is one way. Easy to compute, impossible to reverse.

items.title: Salt
items.say: A random salt per user makes identical passwords look different.

items.title: Slow
items.say: And the algorithm is deliberately slow, so guessing billions is impractical.

scenes.code:
stored = argon2("hunter2" + salt)

login:  argon2(typed + salt) == stored ?
scenes.say: To log you in, it hashes what you typed the same way, and compares.

scenes.text:
Never store the password.
*Store the proof.*
scenes.say: That's password hashing. Never store the password, store the proof.
